_comment: Where tools/title_progress.py finds The Simpsons Game and what cannot be read from its sources. Paths are this machine's checkouts; nothing of the title is in this repository.
name: The Simpsons Game

sys.where: all eight groups, opt-in: branch `any360-sys-test`, `--any360_sys_groups=stateless,files,objects,threads,memory,xam,input,audio`; levels, saves, sound and gamepad checked in game

gfx.where: opt-in: branches `any360-graphics-test` and `any360-sys-test`, `--any360_gpu=true`; 60 FPS in gameplay and 30 on menus and loading screens (the game's own pacing), as with the runtime's GPU
todo: Anti-aliasing: host MSAA smooths the game's data buffers along with its colours (false outlines), so the title runs without it (`--any360_gpu_msaa=1`); it needs MSAA that tells data from colour, or supersampling.

next: Frame rates above 60: the game clock, physics and menus keep their speed; the camera does not yet (see known problems).
Upstream's own roadmap stays valid on top: widescreen, controller prompts, restored content, mod support, Android.
open: Above 60 FPS the camera (right stick) barely turns: the title's camera logic, not the input path (every other input is right).
Loading screens and the heaviest scenes drop to 21-25 FPS: bound by the game's own CPU thread, not by the renderer (1-3 ms a frame).
